title: Cohort-based autotune presets for variable SLOs (draft)
content:
Summary:

This is a working draft proposing a cohort-driven autotune preset system for Optimize that selects batching, cache TTL, and quantization aggressiveness per route/cohort based on observed SLA envelope and token economics. Goal: reduce per-token cost by 10–30% across mixed workloads while keeping P99 latency and tail SLOs within agreed thresholds.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Many customers have routes with highly divergent patterns: short high-frequency requests (search/embedding-like), interactive chat (medium length, conversational), and long-generation batch jobs.
- Current single-presets (global qconfig + one batching policy) either over-optimizes for cost and breaks latency SLOs, or wastes capacity.
- We need a reproducible, low-risk way to offer recommended presets that adapt to route cohorts and can be rolled out gradually.

Key ideas:
1) Cohorting: define cohorts by simple telemetry (median request tokens, 90th pct request tokens, inter-arrival quantile, cold cache rate). Keep cohort definitions shallow so they are robust to noise.
2) Preset family: a small set of named presets (e.g., responsive, balanced, batch-lean, deep-quant) combining batching target, dynamic batch window, cache TTL policy, and qconfig profile.
3) Autosuggest engine: given route telemetry and user SLO preference (latency-priority | cost-priority | balanced), recommend top-2 presets with expected cost/latency delta and confidence band.
4) Safe rollout: canary to subset of traffic, monitored rollback triggers based on error rate and tail latency budgets.

Cohort definitions (proposed, coarse):
- cohort:short-burst => median_req_tokens <= 24 AND 95th_req_tokens <= 64 AND median_iat_ms <= 100
- cohort:interactive => median_req_tokens between 25 and 150 AND median_iat_ms between 100 and 2000
- cohort:long-gen => median_req_tokens > 150 OR 95th_req_tokens > 512
- cohort:sporadic-large => low qps (p50_iat > 30s) but occasional long requests (p95_req_tokens > 1024)

Preset family (human-readable, quick reference):
- responsive (latency-first):
  - batching: target small-batches, target_tokens_per_batch 256, max_batch_latency_ms 12
  - cache: prefix_kv_cache TTL 2s, aggressive cache lookup for repeated prefixes
  - qconfig: fp16 or int8-std with minimal per-token speedups (low quantization)
  - expected delta: +0–5% cost, -20–40% P99 latency (vs naive default)

- balanced (default recommendation):
  - batching: adaptive batching with 100–512 token target, max_batch_latency_ms 25
  - cache: prefix_kv_cache TTL 30s for short sequences, session-level TTL 5m for chat-like routes
  - qconfig: int8-moderate with per-model validated fallback
  - expected delta: -10–20% cost, P99 within SLO for most routes

- batch-lean (throughput-first):
  - batching: large target_tokens_per_batch 800–2000, max_batch_latency_ms 60 (for non-interactive routes)
  - cache: session caching + reuse for common prefixes (TTL 30m)
  - qconfig: int8-aggressive or int4 (if model family validated)
  - expected delta: -25–40% cost, potential +30–100ms P99 tail if used incorrectly

- deep-quant (cost-minimal, experimental):
  - batching: similar to batch-lean but with offline prebatching when possible
  - cache: long TTLs + persistent query-result cache for idempotent calls
  - qconfig: int4-perf with fallback to int8 on quality regressions
  - expected delta: -35%+ cost, risk to quality and rare latency regressions

Spreadsheet model and knobs (linked artifact above):
- "presets" sheet contains per-preset parameter rows and simulated cost model macro (tokens/sec, gpu utilization, per-token GPU cost).
- "cohort-sim" sheet accepts route telemetry (p50 tokens, p95 tokens, qps, ttl_hit_rate) and returns cost/latency vector for each preset.
- Please use the example spreadsheet for A/B scenario comparisons.

Quick rollout experiment plan (4 phases):
1) Offline sims: run cohort-sim across 30 representative routes (mix of customer routes + internal benchmark). Identify top-3 candidates to test.
2) Dry-run: apply presets to 5% of traffic in staging-like environment using traffic replay (INF-3181). Measure P50/P95/P99 and token-cost.
3) Canary: route to 5–10% production traffic for up to 48 hours with automatic rollback triggers (P99 increase > 10% absolute, error rate > 0.5%).
4) Ramp: slow ramp to 50% over 72 hours if no regression, then full rollout to remainder.

Monitoring and KPIs to capture during canary:
- P50, P95, P99 latency (overall and model-level)
- per-token GPU cost and per-request cost
- cache hit rate (prefix + session) and TTL effectiveness
- model output quality signals: user feedback, eval prompt set A/B sample (synthetic metrics: stop token, token-per-turn, rouge-like heuristics)
- error rates and OOM incidents

Risk matrix / mitigations:
- quality regressions from aggressive quantization: maintain robust fallback and continuous evals; require per-model quality gate for int4 usage.
- tail latency spikes from larger batch windows: cap per-route max_batch_latency_ms and enforce fallback to responsive preset under tail breach.
- billing surprises for customers: provide simulated cost delta preview and opt-in canary.

Open questions / decision points:
- Should cohorting live in Optimize UI or be a pre-processing step in the routing layer? (Pros: UI gives visibility; cons: moving parts for operators.)
- What is the minimum telemetry window for reliable cohort assignment? 5m, 1h, 24h? My leaning: start with 1h and fallback to 24h for low-qps routes.
- How do we expose per-preset confidence intervals in the UI without scaring customers? Suggest: show expected delta + conservative lower-bound.

Action items / next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Run sims for 30 canonical routes and produce a compact heatmap (Maya) — due EOD 2025-11-24
- Add automatic fallback hooks to rollout service (ENG ticket INF-3181 assigned to Rafael)
- Author canary runbook and alert thresholds (Priya)
- Prepare short customer-facing one-pager explaining presets and opt-in canary (Evan)

Notes to self / rough checklist:
- Validate int4 perf on A100 vs H100 for model families we deploy (OPT-family, LLaMA variants)
- Add small sample of eval prompts to spreadsheet to detect semantic drift quickly
- Keep presets small set (<=4) to avoid decision paralysis

If you want to review quickly: open the linked spreadsheet and run the "route-sim" macro on the customer_preset_examples tab. Comments inline below.

-- end of draft --

Unresolved ideas I left intentionally loose: automated cohort reclassification triggers (once per day), and a notion of "preset inheritance" where balanced inherits responsive tweaks for certain models. We can iterate after sims.
